summary_paragraph: James, a 60-year-old man with a history of COPD, alcohol use disorder, and tobacco use, was admitted for alcohol detoxification and hypoxemia. He presented with shortness of breath and a history of recent alcohol use, and was found to have worsening bronchial infiltration on chest X-ray suggestive of pneumonia. He was treated with clindamycin, azithromycin, prednisone, and albuterol for pneumonia and COPD exacerbation, and managed for alcohol withdrawal with diazepam, which was tapered as symptoms improved. His oxygen levels stabilized, and he was discharged to extended care with a plan to continue medications and pursue rehabilitation. He expressed a strong desire to remain sober and engage in recovery support, and was given follow-up instructions for PFTs and outpatient workup of atypical white blood cells noted on differential.
